messages:
ana: Heads-up — after the 03/12 kernel-selection tweak I'm seeing a consistent p99 host-side latency bump for small seq requests (<=32 tokens). Starts ~2024-03-12 18:04 UTC.
kevin: Can you paste the flame or a quick profile snippet? is this on hosted or a dedicated pool?
ana: Hosted (prod-us-east). Quick flame from pprof attached inline: \n```
flame: parse_and_deserialize -> host_preproc -> serialize_frame -> net_write (40%)\nshort-path kernel: 5%  heavy-kernel: 30%\nKV cache ops: miss_count spike correlated with parsing windows
```
ana: TL;DR: runtime is choosing the 'heavy' attention kernel for many short requests, which amplifies host parsing + small-write overheads. also seeing more KV cache thrash when requests are chunked differently.
perf-bot: alert: hostlatency.p99 > 120ms for route /v1/complete-sm on prod-us-east (rolling 15m)
kevin: ugh. that kernel selection change was benefiting long seqs, probably using sequence-length threshold too high. current rule: if avg_seq >= 64 -> heavy kernel, else fast. looks like noisy avg due to batching across long/short requests.
sachin: hypothesis: cross-customer batching mixes long and short sequences so the kernel selector biases to the longer kernel; for short seqs the per-token overhead of heavy kernel + host parse wins out. also KV cache keys are per-prefix fragment which fragments warm cache.
maria: can we quick-fix by adding per-request routing: prefer fast kernel if seq_len <= 32 irrespective of batch avg? fallback to heavy only when every item > 64.
kevin: yeah, implement a per-request kernel hint that overrides batch avg when latency-sensitive header x-low-latency=true present. default behavior unchanged.
ana: also propose we change batching heuristic: avoid batching long requests with small ones. iirc we have a 'mix' policy that groups by arrival time only. suggested policy: bucket by seq_len class (<=32, 33-128, >128) then fill batch from same bucket for first N ms, fallback to mix after timeout.
sachin: KV cache note: logs show frequent kv_evicts for these short-controls. sample log lines:\n```
[2024-03-12T18:03:57Z] session=abc shard=12 kvcache: miss seq=18 prefix=tok-0..32
[2024-03-12T18:03:57Z] session=abc shard=12 kvcache: evict prefix=tok-0..16 reason=slot_pressure
```
kevin: so fragmentation from streaming chunking is causing warm entries to be evicted before next chunk arrives. maybe we should normalize prefix keys by coalescing adjacent small prefixes into canonical slot ranges.
maria: Agreed. Two short-term mitigations: 1) increase kvcache soft-reserve for active sessions by +2 slots, 2) use normalized prefix bucketing (round down to 32-token slots) so adjacent fragments hit same bucket.
ana: Perf experiment plan (quick):\n- revert kernel selector rule in canary to per-request hint (kevin)\n- change batching policy in canary to bucket-by-seqlen 0/32/128 (sachin)\n- deploy kvcache bucketing and +2 soft slots to canary (maria)\n- run synthetic microbench: 1k small requests/sec + mixed long requests and measure host p50/p95/p99 and kv hit rate
Commands:\n```
# microbench curl loop (example)
for i in `seq 1 1000`; do 
  curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/complete-sm -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV" -d '{"input":"hi","max_tokens":24}' &
done
# perf tool: run with profile sampling
perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 30
perf script | ./pprof-top -n 20
```
kevin: I'll own the kernel hint canary rollout and a tiny feature flag. estimate 2h to patch + 1h to roll.
sachin: i'll prototype batching bucketer and run local harness against the canary 10.0.12.34:8080. will add metrics: batch_size_by_bucket, avg_seq_by_batch.
maria: i'll patch kvcache bucketing and add metrics for kvcache.hit, kvcache.miss, kvcache.eviction_by_reason. keep default off for 24h then toggle.
ana: cool. can we also add a short-term circuit: if host p99 for route > 200ms, prefer single-request batches for that route for 1m to reduce mixing? saves tail while we triage.
kevin: good idea. add to rollout checklist.
perf-bot: deploy: canary kernel-hint flag enabled on prod-us-east-canary at 2024-03-12T20:10:12Z by kevin
ana: i'll monitor dashboards, will post updates here. tagging @maria and @sachin to confirm when canary metrics look good. :thinking_face:
maria: noted, starting kvcache canary in 10m.
sachin: batching canary running now on test-harness, pushing metrics to /dash/canary/batching in 5m.
ana: thanks team — follow-ups: kevin: kernel rollout, sachin: batching patch PR, maria: kvcache change + metrics. expect status update in this thread in ~3h.
